summary: Kootenai NF lookout site near Libby, MT: an 80-ft steel tower in the 1930s and a 40-ft L-4 tower in 1934, abandoned by 1942; gone, with concrete blocks left on the summit.

facts.design: 40-ft L-4 tower (1934); an 80-ft steel tower is also recorded for the 1930s
facts.status_note: Listed gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association and removed per Forest Lookouts; firelookout.com says abandoned 1942; a 2026 trip report found concrete blocks on the summit and a collapsed hut on Fleetwood Point

access.note: A 2026 trip report walked forestry trail FT-270 to the summit; the signed trailhead is about 70 m north of the pullouts. No source read says whether the site is open to visitors

visit.trail_note: The 2026 trip report walked trail FT-270 from a pullout; the signed trailhead is about 70 m north of the pullouts, and the writer says the sign is easy to miss

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The brief's conflict note records firelookout.com as standing, but the page read says the lookout was abandoned in 1942. It mentions only a patrol cabin with a crow's nest still there in the 1980s, which is not the lookout. Forest Lookouts and the Forest Fire Lookout Association both mark it gone. Kept as gone.

Forest Lookouts gives a 40-foot L-4 tower for 1934 and an 80-foot steel tower for the 1930s; firelookout.com gives only the 80-foot tower. The record keeps 12.2 m (40 ft) for the L-4 tower, and the story covers both.

Firelookout.com puts the 80-foot tower atop Fleetwood Point, 1.25 miles northwest; Forest Lookouts says 1 1/2 miles northwest. The 2026 trip report describes towers on both Alexander Mountain and Fleetwood Point.

notes_for_editor: Gone status is well supported by three sources. Heights and sites disagree: the 80-ft tower and the 40-ft L-4 may be different structures. Forest Lookouts cites a source named Kresek for its dates; not available to check. Forest Fire Lookout Association Facebook posts on the site could not be fetched. Record elevation 1417 m matches firelookout.com's 4649 ft; the trip report gives 1422 m for the summit. Suggest clearing the brief's 'firelookout_com=standing' conflict note.
